paper.title: A General Recipe for the Analysis of Randomized Multi-Armed Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Generic family F with divergence D_pi satisfying Assumption 2
unmapped: Arbitrary family of reward distributions F for which a divergence D satisfies properties (A1)-(A4); noise model is generic, not one of the vocabulary values
Policy must satisfy Assumption 1/4 bounds on sampling probabilities
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cF$ be a family of distributions and $(F_1,\dots, F_K) \in \cF^K$ be a MAB.

$\cF$ is a SPEF if there exists a set $\Theta\subset \R$, a measure $\eta$ and some function $b: \Theta \mapsto \R$ such that ... $\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu_\theta}{\mathrm{d}\eta}(x) = \exp(\theta x - b(\theta))$

settings.name_in_paper: SPEF with means in a known range [mu^-, mu^+]
unmapped: Means belong to a known finite range [mu^-, mu^+]
settings.definition_quote: if the means belong to a known range $[\mu^-, \mu^+]$, \TS{} with Jeffreys prior \citep{korda13TSexp} is also asymptotically optimal on $\cF_b^\Theta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian distributions with unknown variances (means lower bounded by known mu^-, variances bounded by known V)
unmapped: Gaussian rewards with unknown variances; known lower bound mu^- on means and known upper bound V on variances (estimates clipped)
Support [0,B] with B known to the learner (rescaled bounded rewards)
settings.definition_quote: In this part we consider the family of distributions with a bounded support $[0,B]$, that we denote by $\cF_B$.

unmapped: Known convex h with h(|x|)/|x|^{1+eta} -> infinity and known B; E[h(|X|)] < B; additionally E[h(|X|)^{2+eps_F}] < infinity
Known convex h and B; centered moment E[h(|X-mu_F|)] < B (e.g. bounded variance); E[h(|X|)^{2+eps_F}] < infinity; known lower bound mu^- on means

settings.name_in_paper: 1-sub-Gaussian distributions with means in a finite range R
unmapped: Means belong to a finite range [mu_0^-, mu_0^+] of width R
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cF$ be the family of $1$-sub-Gaussian distributions with means in $\cR=[\mu_0^-, \mu_0^+] \subset \R$

algorithms.name: MED (Minimum Empirical Divergence, general version with divergence D_pi and sequence a_n)

bound.regime: for any c > lim a_n (a_n positive), or a_n=0 if D_pi bounded

symbols.D_k: D_pi(F_k, mu_star), divergence of arm k's distribution to optimal mean

extra_assumptions: policy satisfies Assumption 1 or 4 (bounds on sampling probabilities)

source.label: th::main_result
source.quote: Then, for any $c > \displaystyle \lim_{n\to \infty} a_n$, if $(a_n)_{n\in \N}$ is \textbf{positive} it holds that \[\forall k: \Delta_k>0, \quad \bE[N_k(T)] \leq (1+c) \frac{\log(T)}{D_\pi(F_k, \mu^\star)} + o_c(\log(T)) \;.\] Furthermore, the bound holds for $a_n=0$ ... if $D_\pi$ is upper bounded

results.notes: Generic meta-theorem for any randomized policy satisfying the assumptions; bounds expected pulls of a suboptimal arm, not regret directly.

symbols.a_T: value at n=T of the non-increasing non-negative sequence (a_n) used by MED

extra_assumptions: means in finite range R (constant hidden in lesssim)

source.label: lem::pb_ind_sg
source.quote: Let $\cF$ be the family of $1$-sub-Gaussian distributions with means in $\cR=[\mu_0^-, \mu_0^+] \subset \R$, and consider MED implemented with $D: (F, \mu_1) \in \cF \times \cR \mapsto \frac{(\mu_1-\mu_F)^2}{2}\ind(\mu_1\geq \mu_F)$ ... Then ... $\cR_T \lesssim  K^\frac{1}{4}T^\frac{3}{4} \wedge \sqrt{KT\times (\log(K)+a_T^{-1})}$

results.notes: Worst-case over instances; lesssim hides absolute constants and the range R.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

symbols.KL_i: K_inf(F_i, mu_star) = kl(mu_i, mu_star) for SPEF

extra_assumptions: MED uses K_inf divergence of the SPEF

source.label: cor::spef
source.quote: MED implemented with the $\kinf^{\cF_b^\Theta}$ divergence is asymptotically optimal on $\cF_b^\Theta$.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality interpreted as matching the Lai-Robbins/Burnetas-Katehakis lower bound.

bound.expression_latex: \TS{} with Jeffreys prior is also asymptotically optimal on $\cF_b^\Theta$
bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::spef
source.quote: if the means belong to a known range $[\mu^-, \mu^+]$, \TS{} with Jeffreys prior \citep{korda13TSexp} is also asymptotically optimal on $\cF_b^\Theta$.

results.notes: Recovers optimality known for standard TS (Korda et al.) but for TS* variant.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::G
source.quote: MED using divergence $D$ (with clipped estimates) and $a_n = \frac{4}{n}$, and Gaussian \TS{} (Algorithm~\ref{alg::TS_G}) with inverse-gamma priors with shape parameter $\alpha< 0$, are both asympotically optimal for Gaussian distributions with a known lower bound on their means and upper bound on their variances.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::G
source.quote: Gaussian \TS{} (Algorithm~\ref{alg::TS_G}) with inverse-gamma priors with shape parameter $\alpha< 0$, are both asympotically optimal for Gaussian distributions with a known lower bound on their means and upper bound on their variances.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::bounded
source.quote: If the upper bound $B$ is known, then the MED policy using the $\kinf^{\cF_B}$ divergence and $a_n=0$ for all $n$, and the Non-Parametric TS$^*$ algorithm (Algorithm~\ref{alg::NPTS}) are both asymptotically optimal.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::bounded
source.quote: If the upper bound $B$ is known, then ... the Non-Parametric TS$^*$ algorithm (Algorithm~\ref{alg::NPTS}) are both asymptotically optimal.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::h
source.quote: The version of MED implemented with the divergence $D$ presented in Lemma~\ref{lemm::cond_h}, and $a_n=0$ for all $n$, is asymptotically optimal on $\cF_{h,B}$.

results.notes: Requires solving an optimization problem per step.

bound.regime: limsup of R_T/log(T) as T -> infinity

source.label: cor::centered_h
source.quote: The version of MED implemented with the divergence $D$ presented in Lemma~\ref{lemm::cond_h_cent}, and $a_n=0$ for all $n$, is asymptotically optimal on $\cF_{h,B}^c$.

results.notes: First optimal algorithm claimed for centered case (e.g. bounded variance).

symbols.Lambda_k: Lambda_gamma^star(F_k, mu_star), relaxed K_inf with exploration-bonus parameter gamma

extra_assumptions: F defined by centered h-moment condition

source.label: th::npts
source.quote: If $\cF$ is defined by a centered $h$-moment condition (Eq.~\eqref{eq::centered_main}), then for any $c>0$, $\gamma>0$ and for any sub-optimal arm $k$, $h$-NPTS satisfies \[\bE[N_k(T)] \leq \frac{1+c}{\Lambda_\gamma^\star(F_k, \mu^\star)} \log(T) + o_c(\log(T)) \;. \]

results.notes: Bounds expected pulls of suboptimal arm; not necessarily asymptotically optimal since gamma>0.
